chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter the state of Ihram, if you trim the hair of your head or tie it together, then shaving (al-halq) becomes obligatory upon you and shortening (al-taqseer) is not for you. And if you do not do that, then you have the choice between shortening and shaving during Hajj al-Tamattu', and in Hajj al-Qiran (or al-Mufrid, depending on context of 'al-Mut'ah' as a type) there is only shortening."

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لَبَّدَ: To tie or bind the hair

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on trimming hair before entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal consequence of prematurely trimming or tying hair before the designated time of Halq or Taqsir, rendering shaving obligatory to preserve the integrity of the ritual act. It further distinguishes between Hajj al-Tamattu' and Hajj al-Qiran, where shaving is mandatory, versus Hajj al-Ifrad, where shortening is preferred, reflecting the scholarly consensus on the varying obligations based on the type of Hajj performed.
